base_member_text: [L2982-L3009] (HIGH/direct-access record shape) When dtchanged is true qinterp has only three fields although the file record length and reader contract are four fields, unlike the non-interpolated write of q(:,:,:).
audit_member_text: [L2990-L3008] (HIGH/boundary-file schema) When time-step interpolation is active, qinterp has only three fields and the writer omits the fourth elevation field even though the direct-access record length and non-interpolated path use four fields.

base_member_text: [L3524-L3528] (HIGH/incorrect layer flux conversion) Second-order layer flux is converted using q1/z and q2/(h0+z), even though z is negative and the lower and upper layer thicknesses are h0+z and -z respectively.
audit_member_text: [L3524-L3529] (HIGH/layer averaging) The 3D second-order update divides the first-layer flux by z (negative) and the second by h0+z, inconsistent with the layer thicknesses and with the earlier short-wave implementation that uses h0+z for layer 1 and -z for layer 2.

base_member_text: [L2006-L2098] (HIGH/repeated pointer allocation) wp%PRindex is allocated inside the offshore-point loop, so the second point attempts to allocate an already-associated pointer.
audit_member_text: [L2006-L2098] (HIGH/allocation/runtime) wp%PRindex is allocated inside the offshore-point loop, so the second iteration attempts to allocate an already-associated pointer.

base_member_text: [L627-L641] (MED/singular shallow-depth formula) The TMA correction divides by tanh(k*h0) and normalizes by sqrt(sum(y)) without guarding zero boundary depth or a collapsed spectrum.

[L1372-L1381, L1494-L1517, L1728-L1749] (HIGH/zero-energy singularity) Zero-energy spectra are permitted by the readers but derived direction, peak frequency, and representative-period calculations divide by zero-energy sums without a fallback.
audit_member_text: [L489,L641,L1495,L1512,L1637] (HIGH/numerical robustness) Hm0=0 is explicitly accepted, but the resulting zero spectrum reaches unguarded normalizations and weighted means whose denominators are zero.
[L1741-L1749] (MED/numerical robustness) tpDcalc divides by unguarded spectral moments, so an empty threshold mask or zero-energy spectrum produces an undefined representative period.

base_member_text: [L3271-L3342] (HIGH/wrong cutoff index) The superharmonic cutoff tests k3(m,1), but for m>K+1 valid entries start above column 1 and k3(m,1) remains its initialized zero, disabling the intended cutoff.
audit_member_text: [L3341-L3342] (MED/filtering/indexing) The high-wavenumber cutoff tests only k3(m,1), but rows m>K+1 populate columns ii>1 while column 1 remains zero, so those higher rows evade the cutoff.

base_member_text: [L3413, L3417] (HIGH/dimensionally inconsistent layer formula) The upper-layer ratios subtract sinh(KKx) or sinh(KKy) rather than an interface-depth product, leaving a dimensioned wavenumber as a hyperbolic-function argument and omitting z.
audit_member_text: [L3411-L3417] (HIGH/scientific formula) The upper-layer qx2/qy2 ratios subtract sinh(KKx) or sinh(KKy) with no depth factor, unlike the surrounding dimensionless sinh(k*depth) terms, producing dimensionally inconsistent layer partitioning.

base_member_text: [L978-L990, L1175-L1203, L1327-L1336, L1353-L1356] (HIGH/axis/interpolation mismatch) The readers do not sort or reject nonmonotone axes—even noting that SWAN frequencies are often nonmonotone—while endpoint range tests and linear_interp calls assume an ordered frequency axis.
[L1307-L1316] (HIGH/invalid spectral integration) Pre-interpolation variance uses signed local df and dang values on axes described as potentially nonmonotone, so m0 can be negative before sqrt(m0).
audit_member_text: [L965-L998,L1038-L1046,L1311-L1335] (HIGH/spectrum-axis handling) The SWAN reader acknowledges that frequencies are often non-monotone but performs only no-op assignments, after which interpolation and integration assume ordered endpoints and can reject or negatively integrate a descending frequency axis.

base_member_text: [L2061-L2068] (HIGH/zero interpolation divisor) Spatial spectral interpolation rescales by sfimp/sfnow without guarding sfnow=0.
audit_member_text: [L2064-L2068] (MED/numerical robustness) Spatial spectrum interpolation rescales by sfimp/sfnow without guarding sfnow=0.

base_member_text: [L980-L990, L1015-L1046, L1175-L1203, L1241-L1249] (HIGH/unchecked array extent) File-provided frequency and direction counts are not validated, while later code unconditionally accesses angle element 2 and adjacent-angle differences.
audit_member_text: [L1015-L1046,L1189-L1203,L1132-L1143,L1239-L1250] (MED/bounds/input validation) Both spectrum readers index angular entries 1 and 2 without enforcing nang>=2, so a one-direction input can read out of bounds.

base_member_text: [L172-L181, L593-L607, L691, L984, L1019, L1092, L1180, L1193, L1206] (HIGH/reallocation of associated pointers) The catch-up loop can call a spectrum reader repeatedly on the same spectrum object, but the readers allocate its pointer components again without first deallocating or nullifying them.
audit_member_text: [L172-L180,L593-L607,L1092,L1180-L1206] (HIGH/allocation/runtime) The external-time catch-up loop can call read_spectrum_input repeatedly on the same specin element, but each reader unconditionally allocates already-associated pointer components, causing an allocation failure when more than one spectrum interval is skipped.

base_member_text: [L1866-L1877] (MED/time-axis inconsistency) rtin is set to tslen*dtin although the generated axis ends at (tslen-1)*dtin, leaving duration conventions off by one sample.
audit_member_text: [L1866-L1877] (LOW/time-axis contract) rtin is stored as tslen*dtin although the generated tin axis ends at (tslen-1)*dtin, creating a one-step inconsistency in the internal duration.

base_member_text: [L3348-L3350] (HIGH/off-by-one Fourier index) Superharmonic phases access Findex(1)+ii and +jj instead of the component indices Findex(ii) and Findex(jj), shifting every lookup and reaching beyond the last generated component.
audit_member_text: [L3348-L3350] (HIGH/indexing/phase) Second-order component phases use Findex(1)+ii rather than Findex(1)+ii-1 (or Findex(ii)), shifting every primary component by one frequency bin and reading beyond the generated-component span for ii=K.

base_member_text: [L1637-L1657] (HIGH/CDF construction) The trapezoidal cumulative directional distribution is not normalized after integration, so its final value is generally below one although draws span the full [0,1) interval.
audit_member_text: [L1637-L1657] (MED/sampling/CDF) The PDF is normalized by its simple sum but its CDF is then formed with trapezoidal half-endpoint weights, leaving the last CDF value below one and sending some uniform random draws outside the CDF interpolation range.

base_member_text: [L1569-L1572] (HIGH/dispersion formula) The nonhydrostatic frequency cutoff assigns g*k*tanh(kh)/(2*pi) without the square root required to convert dispersion-relation omega-squared to frequency.
audit_member_text: [L1567-L1572] (HIGH/scientific formula) The nonhydrostatic cutoff frequency is computed as g*k*tanh(kh)/(2*pi), omitting the square root required by the dispersion relation and yielding dimensionally incorrect frequency filtering.

base_member_text: [L3436-L3441, L3524-L3530] (HIGH/discarded transverse velocity) The second-order routine computes qy1 and qy2 time series but never adds them to vits or dvits when assembling the nonhydrostatic boundary signal.
audit_member_text: [L3436-L3441,L3524-L3530] (MED/missing state update) Second-order 3D generation computes qy1 and qy2 fields but the accumulation branch updates only uits and duits, leaving vits and dvits without the corresponding transverse second-order contribution.

base_member_text: [L1956-L1959] (HIGH/zero normalization divisor) Per-location variance is rescaled by (hm0/hm0post)^2 without checking hm0post, which can be zero for a location with no selected-frequency energy.
audit_member_text: [L1939-L1959] (HIGH/numerical robustness) Wave-train variance rescales by (hm0/hm0post)^2 without guarding hm0post=0, which occurs when the selected component frequency range contains no energy for a location.

base_member_text: [L3226-L3242, L3406-L3418, L3434-L3447] (HIGH/allocation/branch mismatch) Six-field storage and qx/qy layer arrays are allocated only when nonhq3d=1 and nhlay>0, but later branches test only nonhq3d=1 and can access those arrays when they were never allocated.
audit_member_text: [L3226-L3242,L3407-L3418,L3434-L3441] (HIGH/branch-condition/runtime) Allocation of six-field 3D arrays requires nonhq3d==1 and nhlay>0, but later use tests only nonhq3d==1, so nonhq3d==1 with nhlay<=0 accesses unallocated qx/qy arrays and fields 5-6 of four-field arrays.

base_member_text: [L125-L130] (HIGH/output/state contract) The last-step early return occurs after incrementing bccount and before assigning the INTENT(OUT) curline, so the caller receives an undefined line while the global sequence advances.
audit_member_text: [L125-L131,L331-L332] (MED/state/output contract) The routine increments bccount before the final-timestep early return, and that return leaves the INTENT(OUT) curline unassigned while also consuming a boundary-condition sequence number.

base_member_text: [L299-L321] (MED/resource lifecycle) Cleanup deallocates containers with pointer components without freeing their pointed-to spectra and variance arrays, and it omits vits, duits, dvits, and the nonhydrostatic WDindex, allowing repeated boundary generation to leak substantial storage.
audit_member_text: [L299-L321,L1932-L1938,L2584-L2588] (MED/resource management) Cleanup deallocates pointer-containing parents without freeing their pointed-to Sf arrays and never deallocates vits, duits, or dvits, leaking substantial memory on each regenerated boundary condition.

base_member_text: [L167-L181, L294-L296] (MED/multi-location duration contract) Each location may overwrite wp%rtbc and advance its own end time, while the global end time is advanced only from location 1 and the saved/admin duration is taken from the last location, with no equality check.

[L218-L219, L1682-L1713] (MED/suspicious geometry endpoint) Cyclic direction adjustment derives the boundary span from point max(ny-2,1) rather than the far offshore-boundary endpoint, making the intended ghost-cell/physical-span contract unclear.
[L566-L580] (HIGH/unchecked input divisor) JONSWAP-table Tp is read directly with no positivity validation and is immediately used as 1/Tp and to construct dfj.

[L965-L998] (HIGH/unimplemented format semantics) SWAN RFREQ input is explicitly marked as still needing conversion to absolute frequency, yet both RFREQ and AFREQ branches currently leave the frequency vector unchanged.
[L1380-L1383] (MED/angle normalization) MOD is used to normalize the mean direction, but Fortran MOD preserves a negative dividend and can leave dirm below zero.

[L1425-L1433] (MED/filename sequence overflow) Boundary filenames encode exactly five decimal digits with CHAR(48+i), so bccount above 99999 produces non-digit characters and possible filename collisions or invalid names.
[L1691-L1709] (MED/unguarded geometric division) Cyclic adjustment computes L_wave/sin(alfa_wave) with no branch for a wave parallel to the grid span, relying on floating-point infinity behavior.

[L1775-L1791, L1581-L1600, L1866-L1869] (HIGH/empty frequency selection) If thresholding and fmax remove every component, MAXLOC returns index 1 for both ends, producing dfgen=0 and a later division by dfgen.

[L1866-L1877, L2124-L2148] (MED/FFT frequency mapping) Findex is derived from dfgen even though the actual FFT spacing is 1/(tslen*dtin), and ceiling/even-length adjustments do not ensure those spacings are equal.

[L2241-L2257, L2286-L2304] (MED/lost-energy accounting) Components above the upper directional edge receive WDindex=lntheta+1 and are excluded from all physical theta bins, but the diagnostic counts only WDindex=0 as lost.
[L2452-L2462] (HIGH/zero envelope divisor) Directional envelope amplitudes divide by stdeta without guarding a zero total elevation series.
[L2499-L2516] (HIGH/zero energy rescaling) Energy scaling and directional percentage reporting divide by unguarded mean and total energy, including the bclwonly zero-envelope path.
[L2629-L2645] (HIGH/layer-thickness singularity) The two-layer velocity formula guards nhlay>0 but not nhlay=1, where z is zero and the u2 division by -z is singular.
[L2804-L2823] (HIGH/resonant denominator) The bound-long-wave interaction coefficient divides by a dispersion-mismatch term that can approach or equal zero, with no resonance tolerance or cap.
[L2845-L2850] (HIGH/complex logarithm singularity) Bound-wave phase is obtained with LOG of Fourier coefficients without excluding zero-amplitude components, for which complex log is singular.
[L3160-L3168] (LOW/ignored I/O status) The nonhydrostatic administration-file open and write collect iostat but never test it, so list-file failure is silently ignored.
[L3411-L3417] (HIGH/zero directional-wavenumber divisor) Layer flux ratios divide by sinh(KKx*h0) and sinh(KKy*h0) without limits for axis-aligned interactions where KKx or KKy is zero.

audit_member_text: [L410-L422] (MED/input validation) The WBCTYPE select has no default case, so an unsupported value returns with specin uninitialized and later code dereferences its pointer components.
[L3499-L3517] (HIGH/boundary-file schema) The second-order interpolated q-file path repeats the three-field qinterp versus four-field record mismatch, omitting elevation when dtchanged is true.
dispositions.rationale: span-refuted: The mismatched three-field write is inside nonhspectrum==0, but generate_secondorder is private and its only call in this module is guarded by nonhspectrum==1 at 282-283. par is INTENT(IN), so the cited file-writing branch is unreachable and cannot omit elevation in the actual call path.
